FLASHCARD SET · AGES 4–5 YEARS

Transportation & Vehicles flashcards.

Thirty-two spotter cards for everything that goes: the land vehicles kids ride and see every week — car, bus, train, school bus, tractor, ambulance — the helper trucks that keep a town running, the rails and the cables, the boats that float and the machines that fly, and eleven sheets of construction giants, from road roller to tower crane. Every card names its four vehicles on the picture, so the words go home with the art.

These cards belong to Class 24 · Transportation & Vehicles on the Kiddo School learning path.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Run the vehicle hunt

    Pull a card, name one of its four vehicles, then hunt: spot a real bus, a delivery van, a bicycle from the window or on a walk. Spotting is the transport theme’s heart — every real sighting "checks off" a card.

  2. 02

    Sort by where they go

    Land cards in one pile, water in another, air in a third, construction on the floor. Sorting by where a vehicle travels is a first classification lesson — and every family sorts the tricky ones (a seaplane? an amphibian?) differently, which is the best kind of argument.

  3. 03

    Follow the age pills

    Every card carries an age pill. The everyday vehicles — car, bus, train, school bus, fire engine — are Ages 3+; the specialist machines are Ages 4–5. Start where your child’s eyes already go.

  4. 04

    Count the wheels

    Four wheels on the car, many wheels on the articulated bus, none on the hang glider. Wheel counting turns the whole set into early maths — and a figure-hunt for the vehicles that roll on tracks instead.

      FLASHCARD · TRANSPORTATION & VEHICLES · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Car, Bus, Train & Bicycle Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+Land

      The four rides almost every family meets in one week: the family car, the big bus, the long train and the bicycle with its two wheels and its bell.

      Say it together

      “Car! Bus! Train! Bicycle! The car drives on the road, the bus carries lots of people, the train runs on its tracks, and the bicycle goes round and round on its wheels. Which one have YOU ridden?”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Play the ride report: "who came here today — by car? by bus? on a bike?" Then spot them live from the window and count: two cars… a bus… a bicycle! Naming the rides your child actually takes makes this the most personal card in the set.

      Quick parent note

      These four are the anchor vehicles of the whole transport theme — every other card is a cousin of one of them. The bicycle is also the odd-one-out talking point: it goes on the same road as the car but carries its own power (legs!).

      Teach it, step by step

      Truck, Motorcycle, Tractor & Ambulance Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+Land

      Four vehicles with jobs to do: the truck carries the cargo, the motorcycle zips through traffic, the tractor works the fields and the ambulance rushes to help.

      Say it together

      “Truck! Motorcycle! Tractor! Ambulance! The truck hauls heavy things, the motorcycle goes zoom, the tractor pulls on the farm, and the ambulance goes NEE-NOR to help people. What jobs do you see?”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Match each vehicle to its job: "who carries the furniture? who plows the field? who helps at an accident?" Then spot them on the road — trucks are everywhere once you look. The ambulance opens the helpers conversation: it is a truck-sized first-aid kit with a siren.

      Quick parent note

      This card introduces the big idea that vehicles are tools: each one is shaped by its job. The ambulance also belongs to the helper family the community-helpers class teaches — one siren, two lessons.

      Teach it, step by step

      Tram, Trolleybus, Rickshaw & Cable Car Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 4–5Land

      Four city movers that do not steer themselves: the tram and the trolleybus drink power from wires overhead, the rickshaw weaves through busy streets and the cable car climbs on a rope.

      Say it together

      “Tram! Trolleybus! Rickshaw! Cable car! The tram rides on rails in the road, the trolleybus holds a stick up to the wire, the rickshaw carries people through the bazaar, and the cable car flies up the mountain on a rope!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Watch the wires: which of these four follows a line you can SEE? Tram rails, trolley wires, cable ropes — the city’s tracks are hiding in plain sight. Then the hometown question: which of these have you seen here? Which one would you ride first?

      Quick parent note

      This card teaches "guided vehicles" — machines that follow a path someone built. It is also the card with the rickshaw, which families in Pakistan and across South Asia know intimately: a three-wheeler with a roof and a horn.

      Fire Engine, Police Car, Tow Truck & Garbage Truck Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+Land

      The four trucks that keep a town safe and clean: the fire engine with its ladder, the police car with its lights, the tow truck that rescues broken cars and the garbage truck that eats the trash.

      Say it together

      “Fire engine! Police car! Tow truck! Garbage truck! The fire engine sprays water on fires, the police car keeps us safe, the tow truck carries the broken cars away, and the garbage truck — CRUNCH — takes the trash. Who are the helpers today?”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Spot-a-helper week: every time one of these four passes, say what job it is doing — "the garbage truck is collecting OUR street’s bins!" Then act it out: a toy fire engine rescues the teddy from the sofa mountain. Helper vehicles are the easiest kindness lesson with wheels on.

      Quick parent note

      These are the vehicles children love loudest, and they are the bridge to the community-helpers class: truck + job + the person who drives it. The garbage truck is also the Tuesday-morning highlight of many a preschool week — savor it.

      Teach it, step by step

      Scooter, Skateboard, Roller Skates & Unicycle Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+Land

      Four rides with no engine at all: the kick scooter, the rolling skateboard, the eight wheels of roller skates and the one-wheeled wonder called the unicycle.

      Say it together

      “Scooter! Skateboard! Roller skates! Unicycle! The scooter kicks along the pavement, the skateboard rolls on four little wheels, the roller skates clip-clop in pairs — and the unicycle has only ONE wheel. Balance, balance, balance!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Try the family of balance: scoot between two markers, stomp-stomp in boots as "roller skates," and try standing on one leg — the unicycle’s whole secret. Count the wheels of all four: two, four, eight… one! The unicycle’s "one" is the giggle finish.

      Quick parent note

      This card is powered-by-you transport: no fuel except snacks. It also grows gross motor skills — pushing, balancing, stopping — which is why playgrounds and schoolyards fill up with exactly these four. Helmets before glory, every time.

      Teach it, step by step

      Van, Minibus, Limousine & Convertible Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 4–5Land

      Four cars that show what a little stretching does: the van carries the cargo, the minibus carries the team, the limousine stretches long for special guests and the convertible takes its roof off for sunshine.

      Say it together

      “Van! Minibus! Limousine! Convertible! The van is a box on wheels for packages, the minibus seats a whole team, the limousine is a stretched car — loooong! — and the convertible has no roof. Which one would you ride?”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Sort by "what is it carrying?": the van carries boxes, the minibus carries people, the limousine carries movie stars (pretend), the convertible carries sunshine. Then the design question: WHY is the limousine long? Every vehicle’s shape is the answer to its job.

      Quick parent note

      This is the card of vehicle families — same basic car, four different bodies. Spotting them on the road is a matching game: "that van is delivering… that minibus is a school team… that convertible’s roof is DOWN!" Shapes doing jobs, everywhere.

      Bulldozer, Excavator, Crane & Forklift Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 4–5Land

      The heavy hitters of every building site: the bulldozer pushes, the excavator digs its big arm, the crane lifts steel beams sky-high and the forklift stacks pallets like building blocks.

      Say it together

      “Bulldozer! Excavator! Crane! Forklift! The bulldozer pushes the dirt — vroom, push! The excavator digs a big hole. The crane lifts things UP HIGH, and the forklift beeps and carries pallets. Dig, lift, build!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Act out the site: push cushions with a "bulldozer" push, dig with a spoon "excavator," lift teddy high with a rope-and-chair "crane" (grown-up power). Then watch a real site from a safe distance and name what each machine is doing — push, dig, lift, carry. Every site is the same four verbs.

      Quick parent note

      These four are the construction crew’s heart — and they reappear on the eleven construction spotter cards in fine detail. The forklift is the secret favorite: it is a machine that plays Tetris for a living, and it beeps in reverse like a giant video game.

      Teach it, step by step

      Horse Cart, Sleigh, Wagon & Handcart Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 4–5Land

      Four carts from the days before engines: the horse-drawn carriage clops through town, the sleigh slides over snow, the wagon hauls across fields and the handcart waits for strong hands.

      Say it together

      “Horse cart! Sleigh! Wagon! Handcart! The horse pulls the cart — clip clop! The sleigh slides on snow — swoosh! The wagon rolls on four wheels, and the handcart goes wherever YOU push it. Pull, push, slide!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Pull a box "wagon" of toys across the room, then push the same load on a "handcart" — which is easier? Why? Then the horse-power question: how did people move things before engines? Answer: animals, slides and muscles — all four are on this card.

      Quick parent note

      These four teach history in vehicle form: engines are new, carts are old. The sleigh is also the winter cousin of the wheel — where wheels fail (snow), runners slide. Old-tech cards make the new-tech cards make sense.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Horse Cart, Sleigh, Wagon & Handcart lesson on the Learning Path.

      Metro Train, Monorail, Funicular & Steam Locomotive Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 4–5Land

      Four members of the rail family: the metro train glides under the city, the monorail balances on one beam, the funicular climbs steep hills on a cable and the steam locomotive puffs like a dragon.

      Say it together

      “Metro train! Monorail! Funicular! Steam locomotive! The metro runs UNDER the ground, the monorail rides ONE rail up high, the funicular climbs the mountain on a rope — and the steam train goes CHOO CHOO with real smoke!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Rank them by where they run: under (metro), on one beam (monorail), up (funicular), across (steam train). Then the history pair — the steam locomotive and the metro are both trains, a hundred years apart: what changed? (Smoke out, electricity in.) Trains are the clearest time machine in transport.

      Quick parent note

      Rails are the theme: wheels that cannot wander. The steam locomotive is also the loudest "then" on any card — one CHOO CHOO and every child knows exactly which century it belongs to.

      Teach it, step by step

      Go-Kart, Dune Buggy, Snowmobile & Quad Bike Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 4–5Land

      The adventure four: the go-kart races on its little track, the dune buggy bounces over sand, the snowmobile skims across snow and the quad bike grips any trail with four chunky wheels.

      Say it together

      “Go-kart! Dune buggy! Snowmobile! Quad bike! The go-kart zips round the track, the dune buggy jumps the sand, the snowmobile slides on snow — vrrroom — and the quad bike goes anywhere its four big wheels can grip!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Sort by ground: sand buggy, snow sled, track kart, trail quad — each vehicle matches its playground. Then the wheels question: why are the snowmobile’s wheels GONE? (Runners slide where wheels sink.) Adventure machines are shape-follows-terrain, on four very different floors.

      Quick parent note

      These are the "grown-up toys" kids point at — and they double as a terrain lesson: sand, snow, track and trail each built their own machine. Helmets on every one of them, which makes the safety talk easy: even the riders on this card agree.

      Teach it, step by step

      Tractor, Combine Harvester, Road Train & Articulated Bus Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 4–5Land

      The long-haul giants: the tractor pulls everything, the combine harvester eats whole fields of wheat, the road train hauls three trailers across Australia and the articulated bus bends in the middle to turn corners.

      Say it together

      “Tractor! Combine harvester! Road train! Articulated bus! The tractor pulls the plow, the combine eats the wheat — chomp chomp — the road train is a truck with THREE trailers, and the articulated bus bends in the middle! Long, longer, LONGEST!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Order them by length — then the bend question: how does a bus that long turn a corner? (It bends!) Fold a paper "articulated bus" in half and turn the corner yourself. The road train is also a geography story: it belongs to the huge empty roads of Australia, where one truck does the work of three.

      Quick parent note

      This card is about BIG: the longest vehicles in the set, and two of them articulate — a wonderful word that means "bends in the middle." The combine harvester is the farm’s single greatest machine: it reaps AND threshes AND blows the straw out, all in one pass.

      Teach it, step by step

      Coach Bus, School Bus, Double-Decker Bus & Electric Bus Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+Land

      The bus family, four ways: the coach bus for long journeys, the yellow school bus for the morning run, the double-decker bus with its two floors of windows and the quiet electric bus that hums instead of roaring.

      Say it together

      “Coach bus! School bus! Double-decker! Electric bus! The coach goes far away, the school bus brings us to school, the double-decker has TWO floors — climb the stairs! — and the electric bus goes shhh, no engine roar!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Ride-the-bus pretend: line up chairs, punch paper tickets, ring the bell — "stop please!" Then the counting game: how many wheels does a double-decker need? (Six!) And which bus is the quietest? The electric one hums like a fridge with seats.

      Quick parent note

      The school bus is the most personal vehicle on this card for most kids — their own twice-a-day ride. The double-decker belongs to London, the electric bus to the future, and spotting which bus passes your house is a week-long game in itself.

      Teach it, step by step

      Race Car, Rally Car, Go-Kart Trailer & Armored Vehicle Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 4–5Land

      The speed-and-shield card: the race car lives for the track, the rally car jumps gravel roads, the go-kart trailer hauls the little racer to its track and the armored vehicle is a car wearing armor.

      Say it together

      “Race car! Rally car! Go-kart trailer! Armored vehicle! The race car goes FAST round and round, the rally car jumps the bumps on gravel roads, the trailer carries the little go-kart — and the armored vehicle is a car in a suit of armor. Strong and steady!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Race pretend: count down 3-2-1 and "drive" cushions round a rug track, then swap to the slow safe game — the armored vehicle moves slowly because it is protected, not quick. Fast and strong are two different superpowers; this card has both.

      Quick parent note

      Racing cars teach the shape-follows-speed idea: low, sleek, pointy. The armored vehicle teaches the opposite — thick and heavy for protection. And the go-kart trailer is the quiet lesson: even small racers travel with their own support crew.

      Teach it, step by step

      Boat, Ship, Sailboat & Submarine Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+Water

      The floating four: the little boat for the lake, the giant ship for the ocean, the sailboat that runs on wind and the submarine that dives UNDER the water and vanishes.

      Say it together

      “Boat! Ship! Sailboat! Submarine! The boat floats on top, the ship carries the cargo, the sailboat catches the wind — whoosh — and the submarine goes DOWN, down, under the sea! Glub glub glub.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Float-and-sink lab in the bath: which toys float like the boat, which sink like the submarine? Then the wind test: blow a paper sailboat across the water — wind power, just like the sailboat. And the submarine dive: duck the toy under, periscope up!

      Quick parent note

      Water vehicles move on a different highway — no roads, no rails, just waves. The submarine is the set’s only vehicle that hides, which makes it the favorite by a nautical mile. Float-or-sink is also the first science experiment most children ever run, right in the tub.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Boat, Ship, Sailboat & Submarine lesson on the Learning Path.

      Ferry, Kayak, Canoe & Speedboat Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 4–5Water

      Four river runners: the ferry carries cars and people across the water, the kayak is paddled with a double blade, the canoe glides with a single paddle and the speedboat flies with its engine roaring.

      Say it together

      “Ferry! Kayak! Canoe! Speedboat! The ferry goes back and forth, back and forth, all day. The kayak paddles with TWO blades — splash, splash! The canoe paddles on one side, then the other. And the speedboat goes ZOOM across the bay!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Paddle practice in a chair-boat: a double "kayak" paddle on both sides, then a single "canoe" paddle swapped left-right — discover why one-sided paddling spins you in circles! Then the ferry question: what goes back and forth across the same water all day? The patient workhorse of the water.

      Quick parent note

      The kayak-canoe pair is a fine paddling puzzle: two blades or one, sit inside or kneel. The ferry is the water’s bus — same route, every day, horns and all. Rivers were the first highways, and these four still run them.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · TRANSPORTATION & VEHICLES · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Yacht, Catamaran, Cruise Ship & Lifeboat Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 4–5Water

      The ocean fleet: the yacht sails for the joy of sailing, the catamaran stands on two hulls, the cruise ship is a floating town with a thousand rooms and the lifeboat exists for one brave job — rescuing people.

      Say it together

      “Yacht! Catamaran! Cruise ship! Lifeboat! The yacht glides on the wind, the catamaran has TWO hulls — one, two! — the cruise ship is a whole town that floats, and the lifeboat rushes out to help ships in trouble. What a fleet!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Count the hulls: one on the yacht, TWO on the catamaran — build a "catamaran" from two cups taped together and float it: steadier or wobblier? Then the hero story: the lifeboat crews who launch in storms to save others. Boats have jobs, and the bravest job on the water wears orange.

      Quick parent note

      The catamaran’s two-hull trick (stability!) is real engineering a child can test with cups. The lifeboat connects straight to the helpers theme — and the cruise ship answer to "how many people fit on a boat?" always lands like a magic trick.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · TRANSPORTATION & VEHICLES · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Tugboat, Dredger, Hydrofoil & Paddle Steamer Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 4–5Water

      The harbor’s special four: the little tugboat that pushes giant ships, the dredger that eats mud from the bottom, the hydrofoil that lifts its hull and FLYS on stilts and the old paddle steamer that walks on its own wheels of water.

      Say it together

      “Tugboat! Dredger! Hydrofoil! Paddle steamer! The tiny tugboat PUSHES the giant ship — toot toot! The dredger sucks mud like a vacuum. The hydrofoil rises up on wings and flies over the water! And the paddle steamer goes round and round with its paddle wheels — the oldest dance on the river.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Tug test: can a small toy push a big book across the table? (Slowly… yes — that is a tugboat’s whole job.) Then the hydrofoil question: why would a boat want to LIFT out of the water? (Less splash, more speed.) Harbor boats are the riddle cards of the water set.

      Quick parent note

      The tugboat is the set’s best David-and-Goliath story — small, mighty, essential. The hydrofoil is the bridge to the Air cards: a boat that flies. And the paddle steamer is the steam locomotive’s river cousin, wheeling through the same century.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Tugboat, Dredger, Hydrofoil & Paddle Steamer lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · TRANSPORTATION & VEHICLES · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Airplane, Helicopter, Hot-Air Balloon & Rocket Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+Air

      The sky’s famous four: the airplane with its big wings, the helicopter with its spinning blades, the hot-air balloon drifting with the breeze and the rocket that leaves the whole sky behind.

      Say it together

      “Airplane! Helicopter! Hot-air balloon! Rocket! The airplane flies with wings, the helicopter goes whir-whir-whir on top, the balloon floats like a giant bubble — and the rocket goes 5-4-3-2-1, BLAST OFF, all the way to space!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Fly the fleet: paper-plane "airplane," spinning hand "helicopter," a balloon (real or drawn) drifting up — and the countdown: five, four, three, two, one… BLAST OFF, arms up! Then spot them live: contrails for airplanes, whirring for helicopters.

      Quick parent note

      This is the sky’s front door — the four flyers every child can name by three. The rocket is also the set’s only vehicle that leaves the planet, which makes the countdown the best transition in any preschool day: loud, joyful and occasionally earth-shaking.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Airplane, Helicopter, Hot-Air Balloon & Rocket lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · TRANSPORTATION & VEHICLES · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Jet, Seaplane, Glider & Blimp Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 4–5Air

      Four more ways to fly: the jet that outruns sound, the seaplane that lands on lakes, the glider that flies with no engine at all and the round blimp that floats like the world’s slowest balloon.

      Say it together

      “Jet! Seaplane! Glider! Blimp! The jet goes faster than sound — WHOOSH! The seaplane lands on the water — splash, gently. The glider rides the wind with no engine — shhh, quiet flying. And the blimp drifts along, slow and round, like a giant fish in the sky!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Glide test: throw a paper "glider" with the engine off — how far can silence travel? Then the landing question: where does a seaplane park? (On the lake — no runway needed!) And the blimp riddle: why is it so slow? (It floats; it is in no hurry. Some flying is just floating.)

      Quick parent note

      This card stretches "airplane" into a family: power (jet), water-landing (seaplane), engineless (glider) and floating (blimp). The glider is the physics star — it proves wings work on wind alone — and the blimp is proof that flying does not always mean fast.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Jet, Seaplane, Glider & Blimp lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Transportation & Vehicles (Class 24) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · TRANSPORTATION & VEHICLES · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Drone, Fighter Jet, Cargo Plane & Passenger Plane Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 4–5Air

      The working sky: the drone flies by remote control and films from above, the fighter jet patrols fast, the cargo plane hauls pallets of packages and the passenger plane carries hundreds of travelers over whole oceans.

      Say it together

      “Drone! Fighter jet! Cargo plane! Passenger plane! The drone hovers and takes photos from the sky, the fighter jet zooms like an arrow, the cargo plane carries the mail and the parcels — and the passenger plane takes families on holiday, up above the clouds!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Drone-and-pilot pretend: one hand "flies" the drone (slow, hovering), the other works the "remote." Then the job sort: who carries people? who carries boxes? who flies itself? Today’s sky is a workplace — and this card is its staff photo.

      Quick parent note

      The drone is the newest vehicle in the whole set — most grandparents never saw one as children, which makes this card a then-and-now conversation starter. The cargo plane’s giant mouth (it opens at the nose!) and the passenger plane’s hundred-plus seats round out the sky’s delivery and taxi services.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Drone, Fighter Jet, Cargo Plane & Passenger Plane lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · TRANSPORTATION & VEHICLES · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Space Shuttle, Hang Glider, Gyrocopter & Flying Boat Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 4–5Air

      The specialists: the space shuttle rode a rocket to orbit and came home like a plane, the hang glider hangs beneath a wing and rides the breeze, the gyrocopter spins an unpowered blade above its head and the flying boat is a boat with wings that lands on water.

      Say it together

      “Space shuttle! Hang glider! Gyrocopter! Flying boat! The shuttle flies to SPACE and back, the hang glider soars slow like a big bird, the gyrocopter’s top blade spins in the wind — whirr — and the flying boat lands on the lake like a duck. Specialists of the sky!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Hang-glider arms: lean, arms wide, catch the invisible wind, glide across the room — slowest race ever. Then the spaceship question: which one on this card has been to SPACE? (The shuttle — and it landed like an airplane, gliding home.) Sky specialists each solve one problem: space, silence, smallness, water.

      Quick parent note

      The edge-of-flight card: orbit, breeze, rotor and water-landing. The space shuttle is history now — it retired — which makes it a wonderful museum-conversation card. The flying boat closes the loop back to water-01: a vehicle that is honestly two vehicles at once.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Space Shuttle, Hang Glider, Gyrocopter & Flying Boat lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Transportation & Vehicles (Class 24) class on the Learning Path.

      Road Roller, Mixer, Dump Truck & Paver Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 4–5Construction

      The road crew: the road roller flattens everything flat, the concrete mixer tumbles its drum, the dump truck dumps its load and the asphalt paver lays the smooth black road behind it like a carpet.

      Say it together

      “Road roller! Mixer! Dump truck! Paver! The roller goes sllloooow and FLAT, the mixer spins round and round, the dump truck tips its load — crash — and the paver lays the road, smooth like icing on a cake!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Road-building pretend: a paint roller is the road roller (slow… flat…), a jar spins the "mixing" drum, a toy truck tips the "gravel," and a rectangle block becomes the paver laying the road. Four toys, one finished road. Then spot the real crew flattening a street near you.

      Quick parent note

      This card answers a question every child has asked while watching a street get fixed: who does WHAT? The roller’s drum is also the set’s most satisfying shape — a giant rolling pin that makes roads instead of cookies.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Road Roller, Mixer, Dump Truck & Paver lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · TRANSPORTATION & VEHICLES · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Wheel Loader, Backhoe, Grader & Skid-Steer Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 4–5Construction

      The scoop squad: the wheel loader swallows a heap of gravel in one bite, the backhoe carries a digger on its back, the motor grader scrapes the ground flat as a pancake and the little skid-steer spins on the spot.

      Say it together

      “Wheel loader! Backhoe! Grader! Skid-steer! The loader scoops — CHOMP — a big bite of dirt! The backhoe digs with its back arm. The grader shaves the ground smooth, and the skid-steer — the little one! — turns on one spot like a dancer.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Scoop relay: move "gravel" (pom-poms) with a toy scoop or a dustpan-loader from pile to bucket — loader style, big bites. Then the spin test: hop on one foot and turn in a circle — a skid-steer pivot! Four machines, one skill: the perfect scoop.

      Quick parent note

      All four machines exist for the same verb — move material — which makes this the set’s cleanest compare-and-contrast card. The skid-steer is the crowd favorite: tiny, fast, and able to pirouette in place, the ballet dancer of the building site.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Wheel Loader, Backhoe, Grader & Skid-Steer lesson on the Learning Path.

      Drilling Rig, Pile Driver, Telehandler & Boom Lift Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 4–5Construction

      The deep-and-high crew: the drilling rig bores holes into the ground, the pile driver hammers giant nails into the earth, the telehandler reaches out AND up with its telescope arm and the boom lift carries workers in a basket to the sky.

      Say it together

      “Drilling rig! Pile driver! Telehandler! Boom lift! The rig drills down, down, DOWN into the ground. The pile driver goes BAM, BAM — giant hammer! The telehandler stretches its arm like a telescope — out and UP! And the boom lift lifts people in a basket, higher than the trees!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Reach game: how high can YOUR telehandler reach? Stack, stretch, stand on tiptoe (safely!) — then compare with the machine: its "tiptoes" reach six houses high. And the BAM question: why hammer giant nails into the ground? Because tall buildings need strong grips on the earth.

      Quick parent note

      This card is about direction: down (drill, pile) and up (telehandler, boom lift). Foundations are invisible once built, so the pile driver’s hammering is one of the few construction acts kids actually get to hear — BAM, BAM — a percussion section for the whole street.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Drilling Rig, Pile Driver, Telehandler & Boom Lift lesson on the Learning Path.

      Scissor Lift, Material Lift, Tunnel Borer & Trencher Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 4–5Construction

      The up-and-through crew: the scissor lift folds up like an accordion, the material lift hoists loads up the scaffold, the tunnel boring machine chews a tunnel through a mountain and the trenching machine cuts a long neat ditch in a single pass.

      Say it together

      “Scissor lift! Material lift! Tunnel borer! Trencher! The scissor lift goes up like folding scissors — up, up, up! The tunnel borer eats through the mountain — crunch, crunch — a tunnel! And the trencher cuts a long straight line in the ground, like drawing with a giant pencil.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Scissor-fingers: open and close your hands like the lifting scissors — up they go! Then the tunnel game: crawl through a blanket "mountain" while a partner chants "crunch, crunch, keep boring!" Underground construction is invisible in real life — this card makes it edible.

      Quick parent note

      The tunnel boring machine is the biggest vehicle in the entire set — some are as long as a football field and chew through rock with a rotating face of steel teeth. Kids already know its cousin: the worm in the apple. Same idea, city-scale.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Scissor Lift, Material Lift, Tunnel Borer & Trencher lesson on the Learning Path.

      Pump Truck, Water Truck, Lowboy & Batching Plant Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 4–5Construction

      The support fleet: the concrete pump truck sends concrete through a long folded arm like a straw, the water truck sprinkles the dust flat, the lowboy trailer carries the giant machines to site and the batching plant mixes concrete on the spot.

      Say it together

      “Pump truck! Water truck! Lowboy! Batching plant! The pump truck pours concrete through its long arm — slurp, like a giant straw! The water truck sprays the dust — sprinkle sprinkle. The lowboy carries the BIG machines on its flat back, and the batching plant mixes the concrete right there on the spot!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Straw engineering: sip a drink through a long bendy straw — that is the pump truck’s whole trick, moving liquid concrete along a folding arm. Then the sprinkle test: a spray bottle "water truck" tames the dusty dirt in the sandbox. Every hero machine needs a support crew — this is theirs.

      Quick parent note

      The pump truck’s folding arm can reach the middle of a building from the street — concrete delivered like juice through a straw. And the lowboy answers a spotting question kids ask on the highway: why is that truck so FLAT and low? So the giants can climb on.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Pump Truck, Water Truck, Lowboy & Batching Plant lesson on the Learning Path.

      Street Sweeper, Snowplow, Line Painter & Rail Grinder Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 4–5Construction

      The keepers: the street sweeper brushes the gutters clean, the snowplow shoves the snow aside in white waves, the pavement marking machine paints the road’s straight lines and the rail grinder showers sparks to keep the train tracks smooth.

      Say it together

      “Street sweeper! Snowplow! Line painter! Rail grinder! The sweeper brushes, brush brush brush. The snowplow pushes the snow — whoosh, mountains of white! The line painter draws the road’s long yellow lines, and the rail grinder makes SPARKS on the tracks — the road’s tidy-up crew!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Line-painting pretend: lay masking-tape roads and let your child paint the "yellow lines" with chalk or a brush — straight lines are a real skill the machine does at walking pace. Then the sparks question: why does the rail grinder make fireworks? Grinding metal makes sparks — the train track gets a shave.

      Quick parent note

      These are the maintainers — the machines that exist to keep everything else working, which is a quietly beautiful idea to hand a child: roads need brushing, snow needs pushing, lines need painting. The rail grinder’s sparks are the most impressive tidying-up on Earth.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Street Sweeper, Snowplow, Line Painter & Rail Grinder lesson on the Learning Path.

      Cold Planer, Asphalt Recycler, Curb Machine & Slipform Paver Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 4–5Construction

      The road doctors: the cold planer chews the old rough surface off, the asphalt recycler melts the chewings into new road, the curb machine squeezes out the raised edge of the pavement and the slipform paver pours a fresh smooth lane in one glide.

      Say it together

      “Cold planer! Recycler! Curb machine! Slipform paver! The planer shaves the old bumpy road — scrape, like a giant cheese grater! The recycler melts the old bits into NEW road. The curb machine squeezes out the sidewalk’s edge, and the paver glides along leaving fresh smooth road behind it!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Grater demo (grown-up hands): grate a old crayon stub into shavings — that is the planer’s job, chewing off the old surface. Then the recycle idea: old road is not rubbish — it melts and comes back as new road. Roads can be born again!

      Quick parent note

      This card is the recycling lesson of the construction set: nothing gets thrown away, it gets re-laid. The curb machine is the answer to a question adults rarely ask — how did the sidewalk get its raised edge? Squeezed out, wet-concrete style, by a machine that writes curbs the way a pen writes lines.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Cold Planer, Asphalt Recycler, Curb Machine & Slipform Paver lesson on the Learning Path.

      Articulated Hauler, Motor Scraper, Pipe Layer & Trench Compactor Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 4–5Construction

      The earthmovers: the articulated hauler bends in the middle to carry tons over bumps, the motor scraper shaves the ground into its own belly, the pipe layer lowers pipes into trenches like thread through a needle and the trench compactor stamps the ground hard as a drum.

      Say it together

      “Hauler! Motor scraper! Pipe layer! Compactor! The hauler bends in the middle — clunk — and carries a whole mountain of dirt! The scraper shaves the ground flat. The pipe layer LAYS THE PIPES in the ground — the water’s secret roads! — and the compactor stamps, stamp, stamps the earth hard.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Bendy-hauler craft: tape two toy trucks together with a paper hinge — it bends like the real articulated hauler. Then the underground question: where does the tap water come from? Pipes! And the compactor game: stamp the sandbox earth with both feet — firm ground holds roads up.

      Quick parent note

      The articulated hauler is the construction card’s bend-in-the-middle repeat — the same clever hinge as the articulated bus, doing far harder work. And the pipe layer reveals infrastructure’s secret: beneath every road, a whole water-and-sewage city that this card makes visible.

      Teach it, step by step

      Vacuum Excavator, Crawler Carrier, Tracked Carrier & Material Handler Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 4–5Construction

      The clever movers: the vacuum excavator sucks soil like a giant vacuum cleaner, the crawler carrier walks on tank treads over soft ground, the tracked carrier hauls loads where wheels would sink and the material handler’s grab-arm picks and places like a claw machine.

      Say it together

      “Vacuum excavator! Crawler carrier! Tracked carrier! Material handler! The vacuum sucks the dirt — SCHLOOP — no shovel needed! The crawler WALKS on its tank feet — step step step over the mud. And the material handler has a claw — grab, lift, place! Like the biggest claw machine in the world.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Claw machine pretend: a clothes-peg "grabber" picks up pom-poms and places them on a tower — grab, lift, place, exactly the handler’s verb set. Then the tracks question: why TANK FEET instead of wheels? On soft mud, wheels sink; treads walk. Nature thought of it first — snowshoes!

      Quick parent note

      The vacuum excavator is the set’s most surprising machine: digging without touching, so buried pipes stay safe. And the material handler brings the arcade to the building site — every child who has ever steered a claw machine knows this machine’s exact joy and heartbreak.

      Teach it, step by step

      Tower Crane, Crawler Crane, Rough-Terrain Crane & Truck Crane Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 4–5Construction

      The crane family: the tower crane stands like a giant over the whole city block, the crawler crane rolls on treads and lifts the heaviest loads, the rough-terrain crane hops over mud and the truck-mounted crane drives itself to every small job.

      Say it together

      “Tower crane! Crawler crane! Rough-terrain crane! Truck crane! The tower crane is the TALLEST — it watches over the whole city! The crawler walks on treads and lifts the heaviest things. The rough-terrain crane climbs the mud, and the truck crane drives itself to little jobs. Lift, lift, lift!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Crane height sort: which one is tallest? (Tower crane — its top is often higher than the building it builds!) Then the balance game: hold a book at arm’s length — heavy, right? Cranes do that all day with a counterweight on the other side. Build a spoon crane: spoon arm, cup counterweight, lift a pom-pom load.

      Quick parent note

      Four cranes, four answers to one question — how do we lift the heaviest things into the sky? The tower crane is the skyline’s signature and the crawler crane is its strongest. Kids spot cranes from farther than any other machine: they are the flagpoles of construction.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Tower Crane, Crawler Crane, Rough-Terrain Crane & Truck Crane lesson on the Learning Path.

      Generator, Light Tower, Compressor & Welding Truck Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 4–5Construction

      The power crew: the generator trailer hums out electricity for the whole site, the light tower trailer lifts its lamps to turn night into day, the compressor trailer breathes out air for the tools and the welding truck brings the sparks and the steel together.

      Say it together

      “Generator! Light tower! Compressor! Welding truck! The generator makes the electricity — hummm. The light tower lifts its lamps — the site glows at night! The compressor squeezes air for the tools — psshhh. And the welding truck joins the steel with sparks — bzzzz, fireworks at work!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Night-shift pretend: a torch on a chair is the light tower — the whole site glows. Then the sound hunt: the generator HUMS, the compressor PSHHH-es, the welder buzzes — the site has a soundtrack. And the big idea: before the builders build, someone brings the power.

      Quick parent note

      The quiet heroes of the construction set: none of them build anything, and none of the others could build without them. Power, light, air and sparks arrive on four trailers — which is a lovely first lesson in how work really gets done: the support crew comes first.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Generator, Light Tower, Compressor & Welding Truck lesson on the Learning Path.
